name: arg5-targeted-negative-oracle
purpose: Deterministically distinguish an ARG-5 ownership-claim semantic RED from datastore or harness infrastructure failure.
rationale: The classifier has one current call path and owns no durable state, scheduling, retries, or external effects.
Its stable mechanism is a pure evaluation of content-addressed phase artifacts, so an engine protocol would be premature.

boundary.owns: Bundle shape, phase ordering, exact test sets, semantic failure classification, mutation binding, and hash verification
boundary.mechanism: Map one frozen ARG-5 harness bundle to a deterministic gap count and typed failure list
policy_outside: LakatoTree prediction registration and verdict promotion
Which future requirements warrant targeted controls
boundary.state_authority: The immutable artifact bundle is the sole input authority; the module owns no mutable state

invariants: Identical artifact bytes and judge bytes produce identical output.
Pool, connection, container, and timeout failures never count as semantic mutation sensitivity.
Metric zero requires current GREEN, exact targeted ARG-5 assertion RED, restored GREEN, and exact hash bindings.
failure_model: Missing, malformed, hash-drifted, wrong-phase, or infrastructure-failed evidence yields one or more explicit gaps and no mutation.
verification: Synthetic positive bundle returns zero gaps.
Injected PoolError returns nonzero gaps and the targeted infrastructure classification.
The disposable-datastore CI bundle is judged after producer completion.
promotion_gates: At least two independent harness families share a stable bundle protocol.
Durable admission, concurrency, recovery, or single-writer state becomes part of the classifier contract.
falsifiers: If the targeted control can pass after removal of ON CREATE ownership, the test is not mutation-sensitive.
If infrastructure exceptions can yield metric zero, the module contract is false.
